findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring offsets
findings.body: The matcher extracts the grant shortcut with `items[0].substring(3, 5)`, but the encoded prefix is sessionType(2)+tokenType(2)+grantType(2), so the grant shortcut lives at indices 4..6; indices 3..5 straddle the token-type and grant-type shortcuts. In addition the comparison is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` fails the match when the shortcut *does* equal the expected value. As written the matcher accepts any token id whose prefix differs from the expectation and rejects correct ones, so all the new assertions on Details.TOKEN_ID verify nothing (or the wrong thing). Should be `substring(4, 6)` and `if (!...equals(...)) return false;`.

findings.title: Null check for rawTokenId checks grantType instead
findings.body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` duplicates the previous grantType check, so a null `rawTokenId` is never rejected. A null raw token id then silently produces a token id like "onrtac:null" during encoding instead of failing fast.

findings.title: Removal of public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) breaks SPI compatibility
findings.body: The copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` was deleted from the public SPI class `OAuth2GrantType.Context` in server-spi-private. Any custom grant-type provider (or internal code built against previous versions) using it will no longer compile/link. If it is no longer needed internally, this should at least be noted as a breaking SPI change, or kept and made to copy the new `grantType` field.

findings.title: Lazy shortcut registration bypasses duplicate-shortcut validation
findings.body: `getShortcutByGrantType`/`getGrantTypeByShortcut` add entries to both maps at runtime without checking whether the shortcut is already mapped to a different grant type (the only duplicate validation happens once in postInit). A newly deployed grant with a colliding shortcut will silently overwrite `grantsByShortcuts`, so token ids encoded with that shortcut will decode to the wrong grant type.

findings.title: Unused import added
findings.body: `org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory` is imported but not referenced; the grant type is set via `OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE`. Remove the import.
